issues.legal_issue: A law authorizing compulsory acquisition for street widening provides for compensation when it requires payment for the owner's loss and expenses, even if adjustments for benefits may reduce the amount ultimately payable.
material_facts: The acquisition involved land within the prescribed line of a public street, and the owner could be required to remove the building or part of it occupying that land.
The law required compensation for the owner's loss and expenses resulting from the acquisition.

The law required increases or decreases in the value of the remaining property to be considered, and allowed recovery of a betterment charge if the increase exceeded the loss and expenses; those adjustments followed determination of the loss.
issues.conclusion: The law provided for compensation for property acquired under the street-widening power; the possible reduction of compensation, or payment of a betterment charge in rare circumstances, did not negate that provision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 299 of the Government of India Act, 1935, and Article 31 of the Constitution required a law authorizing compulsory acquisition to provide for compensation. Sections 216(1) and 389(1)(f), read together, required full monetary indemnification for loss or deprivation caused by acquisition. Adjustments for the effect of the setback on the remaining property operated only after the loss was determined and did not mean that the law failed to provide compensation.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_chal: A proceeding challenges whether a law authorizing compulsory acquisition meets constitutional compensation requirements.
predicates.law_requires_full_indemnification: The law requires the acquiring authority to compensate the owner for loss or expenses caused by the acquisition.
predicates.loss_is_assessed_before_benefit_adjustme: The law applies adjustments for benefits to the remaining property only after the owner's loss has been assessed.

issues.definition: When a compensation challenge concerns a compulsory-acquisition law that requires full indemnification and assesses loss before benefit adjustments, the law provides compensation.

issues.legal_issue: A law specifies the principles and manner for determining compulsory-acquisition compensation when it requires full indemnification, provides for an appropriate inquiry, and permits civil-court review of the determination.
material_facts: Street widening could require acquisition of very small, irregular, or otherwise unusual pieces of land for which a single standard valuation method might not be appropriate.
The law set full indemnification for the owner's loss or deprivation as the goal of compensation.
An authorized official was required to hold an inquiry and determine compensation, with appeals to a civil-court judge and a further appeal to the District Court.
The appellate courts were not subject to limits on determining compensation justly and appropriately.
issues.conclusion: The law specified both the principles and the manner for determining compensation because it required full indemnification using valuation methods appropriate to the property and provided for an inquiry and judicial appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Section 299 of the Government of India Act, 1935, and Article 31 of the Constitution required the law to specify the principles and manner of determining compensation. Sections 216 and 389 established full indemnification as the governing goal; sections 390, 391, 411, and 434 provided for an inquiry and civil-court appeals, importing judicial norms into the determination. The Court relied on State of Gujarat v. Shri Shantilal Mangaldas & Ors. for the meaning of specified principles as general guiding rules and for the use of differing valuation methods according to the property acquired.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_chal: A proceeding challenges whether a law authorizing compulsory acquisition meets constitutional compensation requirements.
predicates.law_sets_full_indemnity_as_goal: The law makes full indemnification for the owner's loss or deprivation the goal of compensation.
predicates.compensation_is_reviewable_by_civil_cour: The law permits civil courts to review and determine the appropriate compensation on appeal.
predicates.initial_compensation_inquiry_is_required: The law requires an authorized official to hold an inquiry before determining compensation.

issues.definition: When a compensation challenge concerns a law that aims at full indemnification and provides both an initial inquiry and civil-court review, the law specifies compensation principles and manner.
